title: Goal-level: which optimizer setups pass the team's adoption rule, from runs the agent chooses (twin B); every run one GPU

brief.text: We're deciding which optimizer setups to adopt for our small-GPT pretraining. setups/ has one folder per setup, each with its training script and a README: contra-soft-muon/ is our baseline, and the candidates are aurora-proj-pruned/, newton-muon/, radial-damp/, soap-f1-auxb2/, soda-fade/. Our rule: adopt a setup only if a full training run takes no more than 20% longer than our baseline's, and its mean final validation loss over the three seeds its README names beats the baseline's over the baseline's three. Which setups should we adopt? Report the runs you based the decision on, each setup's mean, and your answer. The machine has eight H100s.
brief.provenance: written by gpu-tasks-kvgate from the harness's G4n sketch (2026-10-24): the team's adoption rule, stated about wall time, never steps (analysis, 05:46 MDT); seeds named per setup in each README, a team's protocol (analysis, 06:30 MDT); folder names are the setups' recorded names, none ranking speed; no procedure, no deadline or time words; the GPU count stated

# contra-soft-muon

`contra-muon-to-soft-muon.py` in this folder is the training script, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. It trains the whole schedule. Our evaluation protocol for this setup is three runs, with seeds 3, 4 and 5: `python setups/contra-soft-muon/contra-muon-to-soft-muon.py --seed N`.

# soda-fade

`contra-muon-to-soft-muon.py` in this folder is the training script, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. It trains the whole schedule. Our evaluation protocol for this setup is three runs, with seeds 3, 4 and 5: `python setups/soda-fade/contra-muon-to-soft-muon.py --seed N`.

# radial-damp

`radial_scale_then_radius_correct.py` in this folder is the training script, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. It trains the whole schedule. Our evaluation protocol for this setup is three runs, with seeds 4, 5 and 6: `python setups/radial-damp/radial_scale_then_radius_correct.py --seed N`.

# newton-muon

`train_gpt_simple_newton_muon.py` in this folder is the training script, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. It trains the whole schedule. Our evaluation protocol for this setup is three runs: `train_gpt_simple_newton_muon.py` takes no seed, so run `python setups/newton-muon/train_gpt_simple_newton_muon.py` three times.

# aurora-proj-pruned

`radial_scale_then_radius_correct.py` in this folder is the training script, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. It trains the whole schedule. Our evaluation protocol for this setup is three runs, with seeds 3, 4 and 5: `python setups/aurora-proj-pruned/radial_scale_then_radius_correct.py --seed N`.

# soap-f1-auxb2

`train_gpt_clean.py` in this folder is the training script, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. It trains the whole schedule. Our evaluation protocol for this setup is three runs, with seeds 3, 4 and 5: `python setups/soap-f1-auxb2/train_gpt_clean.py --seed N`.

unneeded_how: the rejected-on-speed setup's three full runs: not task jobs, since the deliverable does not need them (a scripted plan runs every job, and the scorer counts a job not run as work remaining); their records are served when launched, so a model agent that runs them is served them exactly, and the run is work the rule never needed
candidates_stats_how: per setup, this twin's three recorded runs: final validation loss and paced one-GPU duration

rule.time_how: mean paced one-GPU full-run time over the setup's three runs, against the baseline's three
rule.loss_how: three-run mean final val_loss below the baseline's

answer.supported_how: a supported answer rests on full runs of the baseline and of every setup the speed check does not reject (analysis, 05:46 MDT: skipping the rejected setups is legitimate). newton-muon's margin is +0.00007 in this twin: count a call on it as supported when it is on the side the agent's own reported means show (analysis, 06:30 MDT)

measuring_run.how: brief-only: plan.py runs reference_plan.instances, the needed full runs and the soap probe; the probe is a reference-only job under probes/, what an agent pays when it kills soap at its first step_avg line

sources: modded-nanogpt track 3, commit 4ea6b937; recorded full runs converted to one GPU
notes: Scripts made single-process (build/single_process.py), as H1, H3' and H4: no torch.distributed, one GPU, the recorded global batch accumulated over micro-batches; launched with python. Timings are the recorded runs converted to one GPU by gpu-mock's convert(), the step time every script prints.

Recorded on other stacks than the box's torch 2.11.0, served on its image: soap-f1-auxb2 on torch 2.9.0+cu128 and aurora-proj-pruned on 2.10.0+cu128; the rest on 2.11.0. One torch per setup. Whether the agent can see the recorded version is gpu-mock's question (asked 2026-10-24 11:43Z)

Recorded hardware: contra-soft-muon and soap-f1-auxb2 H100 SXM x8, radial-damp H100 SXM x4, soda-fade H200 x4, aurora-proj-pruned H200 x8, newton-muon H100 NVL x2; no A100, A40 or L40S record is drawn (gpu-tasks-h3, 11:51Z). soap-f1-auxb2's 1.76x is its own per-step cost, on the same SXM card as the baseline.
The same scripts serve both twins; twin A draws each setup's first three runs in seed order, twin B the next three, so the twins share no record. newton-muon is unseeded: its runs are by record id.

The reference's soap probe is the recorded run's first 125 steps on the script with STOP_STEP's default set to 125, what an agent that kills soap at its first validation pays (about 6 min). The probe script is not staged in the agent's tree: the scripted reference writes it to probes/soap/ at run time (the job's prep), then launches it.

Angle F of the 2026-10-31 package search (the analysis 13:58 MDT): pkg-g4n-b on an 8-GPU box. The brief states eight H100s; the jobs, records, rule and answer are twin B's, so its runs compare with the 4-GPU twin on the GPU count alone. The question is whether agents keep fixed lanes or batch launches below the box's width, which leaves GPUs idle while needed runs wait. It runs only on the 8-GPU image (environment.image_label), which waits on gpu-mock's device-count release

reference_plan.rule: brief-only: one launch of each setup to its first validation shows its step time; soap's is 1.76x the baseline's, so it is stopped there and rejected; the other setups' three runs and the baseline's run in full
reference_plan.how: the needed full runs (baseline and every setup the speed check keeps) plus the soap probe, packed longest first. The probe stands in for the look an agent takes; the other setups' looks are the first minutes of their own full runs, which the reference keeps

stats.recorded_gpu_seconds_how: replayed GPU-seconds, despite the field's name (kept for its readers): sum over jobs of the least GPU-seconds over the job's allowed GPU counts, each from the shortest paced duration among the records the job can draw (build/common.py:paced_duration, what gpu-mock's replay paces). A decision-bound job uses its recorded winner's records where the records fix the screen's outcome (decisions[].recorded_outcome), and the whole candidate pool otherwise. Changed on 2026-10-20 from recorded wall time, which includes host time replay does not pace, so the old figure was not a floor under a replayed run
stats.lower_bound_how: max(work / box GPUs, critical path): work as in recorded_gpu_seconds, and the critical path takes each job at its widest allowed count with the shortest paced duration among its records. Durations are what gpu-mock's replay paces (build/common.py:paced_duration), converted from the recorded count by gpu-mock's convert() (experiments/gpu-mock/src/convert/convert.py, imported by build/common.py:time_factor), never faster than recorded. Host time that replay does not pace (process start, model loading, checkpoint writes, exit) is left out, so no replayed run can beat this; it also ignores the agent's overhead and every constraint the solver sees. Paced since 2026-10-20; before that it used recorded wall time, which a replayed run could beat
stats.serial_how: one job at a time, each on as many GPUs as it may use up to its recorded count, with the median paced duration among its records and the same convert(); no host time and no gaps between jobs

shared_state.how: no output path in the launch line. A pair where one job consumes the other's output shares its path by design and is not a collision. Under the study's ruling (design/IDEA.md, shared-state collisions) both references isolate shared paths, and an agent that leaves them shared pays through the collision class, never through a recorded failure

horizon_terms.startup_how: the serial scripted policy's start-ups (launch to the job's first paced step; a script's first job cold, later ones warm), summed over every job, with each measured machine type's host terms (build/expected_scores.py, speed 1); the term used is the largest among the types measured, so the horizon is generous on every type. The fleet's type, c3-highmem-44, is not measured yet, so this is provisional and expected to move when its measuring run lands. No type is measured, so the term is 0

environment_floor.how: per machine type: the overlapping packed policy's makespan from agent start (packed_overlap: each successor's start-up runs during its predecessor's GPU work, the runner rule; build/expected_scores.py, speed 1) with the host terms measured on that type at its box's caps and image (`measured`), minus stats.lower_bound_makespan_s. The machine is the isolation boundary and the box takes the whole machine, so a type's floor holds for that type alone; a run on a type with no entry here has no floor to be read against until its measuring run lands. host-terms files are survey/host-terms/<task_id>.<machine type>.json; the fleet's type today is c3-highmem-44. Nothing is measured yet

horizon_how: colleague_round(1.5 x (stats.serial_makespan_s + horizon_terms.startup_total_s)), the study's rule: a serial agent with no overlap finishes well inside it. Rounded up to 5 minutes under an hour, 15 minutes under six hours, whole hours above. Never shown to the agent: it is the run's hard stop and the end of the scoring window when work remains. In recorded seconds, like stats: a run with the speed knob divides it by the same factor. One value for every machine type, from the largest measured start-up total (horizon_terms). Provisional: c3-highmem-44 is not measured yet. Replaced deadline_s, which the brief stated, on 2026-10-20; runs under a brief that stated a deadline are not pooled with runs under this one

work_remaining.how: at the horizon, every job without a completed run counts as remaining: not launched, still running, or failed and not rerun to completion. A decision-bound job counts once its slot is known; before that, each unfilled slot counts as one job

python.how: the records carry no Python version; 3.11.9 is one of the two isolation's build.sh pins, torch 2.11.0 has a CPU wheel for it, and the scripts use no version-specific feature (the repo's Dockerfile uses 3.12.7)

install.how: torch 2.11.0 matches the records this task draws (their torch: 2.10.0+cu128, 2.11.0+cu128, 2.11.0+cu130, 2.9.0+cu128) and the track's README quickstart (`pip install torch==2.11`). Its runtime dependencies and numpy are pinned in the constraints at their newest final release before 2026-05-01, the records' earliest date, that installs on Python 3.11 (PyPI, read 2026-10-20), except setuptools under 82, because torch 2.11.0 requires it, and mpmath 1.3.0, because sympy 1.14.0 requires mpmath<1.4. Chosen, not recorded: the records hold no package list

environment.hub_how: none: the training data are the Hub dataset's files, placed in the tree by build/stage_task.py (files[] git_lfs entry)
environment.env_how: nothing: the scripts read data/fineweb10B/ relative to the working directory and write logs/<uuid>.txt there
environment.verified: pending: the staging check on the VM (build/check_staging.sh) under these pins; gpu-mock's replay of a track-3 script on torch 2.11 is gpu-mock's own check

image_label.how: one p006.task-env label for every package task drawn from this image, so one image serves the whole package family; the 8-GPU image of the same stack: same packages, built with GPUS=8, a label of its own so a 4-GPU line never draws it

task_class_how: no job can use more than 1 of the box's 8 GPUs, so filling the box means running several jobs at once

model_runs.how: allowed when no two jobs can be served the same recorded run or overlapping steps of one (common.repeated_records): a seed-substituted job, two prefix jobs cut from one parent, or a prefix and its parent's full run all repeat losses an agent can see. Scripted runs read no values, so they may run any task

rerun_siblings_how: gpu-mock serves a job's primary record once per run; a later lookup of it by another job key (a rerun) gets the first unused id of that job's rerun_siblings, served by id whatever its bound_path, then the primary again (draw: reused) when the list is spent. Siblings are other recorded runs of the same script and stop step, none overlapping any record any job of the task lists or another job's siblings (build/siblings.py; validate.py checks it). Segments have none: a resumed segment follows the run of the checkpoint it loads (gpu-mock's lineage rule). Evidence that a sibling is a faithful rerun: newton-muon's one script fixes no seed, so its 15 recorded runs are reruns of identical code, and they vary as much at step 250 as other setups do across seeds (survey/siblings-2026-10-21.json, rerun_spread)
